meera: hey all — Meera here, starting runtime dev onboarding. following the "dev-from-source" guide but hitting a link/runtime error when building. who's best to ask for quick help?

alex: welcome Meera! pinging eng-runtime is fine, alex/jeremy usually help infra stuff. can you paste the error output?

meera: sure, pasted below (sorry for the long block)
```
ERROR: /home/meera/workspace/runtime/BUILD:42:1: Linking of rule '//runtime:serve' failed (Exit 1): gcc failed: error executing command ...
/usr/bin/ld: undefined reference to `cuInit'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
INFO: Build completed, 1 test FAILED, 1 target failed.

nvidia-smi reports: NVIDIA-SMI 525.60.13 Driver Version: 525.60.13 CUDA Version: 12.1
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version -> NVRM version: 470.161.03
```

sam: looks like a driver vs userlib mismatch — kernel module is 470 while userland is 525. you usually get undefined `cuInit` when libcuda.so doesn't match the kernel module. quick checks: run `uname -r`, `nvidia-smi`, and `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version`. also check `ldconfig -p | grep libcuda` and `readlink -f $(which nvcc)` to see what CUDA_HOME points to. did you install drivers via apt or the .run?

meera: installed via apt (ubuntu package nvidia-driver-525). rebooted after install. `uname -r` = 5.15.0-78-generic. `ldconfig -p | grep libcuda` shows libcuda.so.1 -> /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (from 525). but /proc/driver/nvidia/version still reports 470.

jordan: when /proc shows an older kernel module it's usually an old DKMS module still loaded. try `sudo dkms status` to see installed modules, and `sudo modinfo nvidia | grep -i version` to see which module is currently loaded. if it's stale, purge older nvidia packages and reinstall, then reboot. alternatively, use our dev container to avoid host driver issues: `docker run --gpus all -it --rm gcr.io/redwood-runtime/dev:cuda-12.1-2025-02 /bin/bash` — that image has matching drivers and CUDA libs for local builds.

alex: another build tip: if you switch drivers, run `bazel clean --expunge` to drop any cached link artifacts. sometimes `bazel build //runtime:serve --spawn_strategy=local` helps with linking on a dev machine. also ensure `CUDA_HOME` and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` are set to the toolkit in /usr/local/cuda-12.1 if you installed CUDA toolkits separately.

meera: ran `sudo dkms status` — shows nvidia, version 470.161.03 installed and built for current kernel. apt thinks 525 is installed but the kernel module for 525 didn't get built. reinstalling drivers now with `sudo apt-get purge 'nvidia-*' && sudo apt install nvidia-driver-525` then rebooting.

devx-bot: DevX tip: New runtime devs — if you want a reproducible environment, use the dev container image (gcr link above) or follow the "Local build troubleshooting" doc: https://redwood.internal/devx/runtime-onboarding. If blocked >2h, page #oncall-runtime.

meera: switched to the dev container, build started and progressing — looks promising. thanks for all the pointers. I'll follow up if it still fails after trying the host reinstall. :thumbsup:

alex: welcome aboard! if you keep hitting host driver funk, ping me or page oncall. also add your laptop type in #new-hires so IT knows.

meera: will do, thanks everyone.
